portInfo.description: Skala is the port-town base; Chora wraps around the hilltop Monastery of Saint John. The cave is another religious site, not a room inside the monastery. Grikos’s Petra/Kalikatsou landscape and Kampos offer alternatives or a longer-day addition without pretending the whole island is walkable from the pier.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Monastery of Saint John the Theologian — Hilltop monastery, Chora, Patmos. Active religious site; check visitor periods and modest-clothing requirements. Allow 90 minutes; official source.
Cave of the Apocalypse — Cave of the Apocalypse complex, Patmos. A distinct pilgrimage visit with steps; worship access must be respected. Allow 45 minutes; official source.
Chora historic settlement — Chora lanes around the monastery, Patmos. White houses, historic mansions and uneven lanes make a separate town walk. Allow 75 minutes; official source.
Skala waterfront — Skala harbour promenade, Patmos. Port-town cafés and market streets support a genuinely local short day. Allow 60 minutes; official source.
Grikos and Petra/Kalikatsou — Grikos bay and Petra rock area, southeastern Patmos. A road outing; the rock is viewed as a landscape, not an encouraged unsafe climb. Allow 90 minutes; official source.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: For Kampos, specify Ano village square or Kato beach; for the religious circuit, specify the cave separately from the hilltop monastery. A vague “Patmos monastery pickup” is not enough.

gettingThere.distanceToCity: Budget 45 minutes for clearance/tender and a vehicle from Skala towards the cave/Chora, and up to 60 minutes for the original interface return. The municipality gives Grikos about 4.5 km and Kampos about 6 km from Skala, but does not label these as measured road or walking distances; this guide does not do so either.
